scripts: Creates the 7 lab users and 9 groups. Asks you to confirm the tenant first.
Deletes only the tagged lab users and groups.

blocks.p: Use a tenant you own for practice: a Microsoft 365 developer tenant, or a new tenant created from an Azure free account. **Never run the scripts in an employer's tenant.** The seed script stops if a tenant has more than 50 users.

blocks.note: See [Create a new tenant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/create-new-tenant) in Microsoft's documentation.

setup.title: Use an admin account in that tenant

blocks.p: You need to create users and groups: User Administrator plus Groups Administrator, or Global Administrator. The account that creates a new tenant is a Global Administrator.
PowerShell 7 is recommended. Windows PowerShell 5.1 also works. Install just the four modules the scripts use:

setup.title: Download the scripts into one folder

blocks.note: Read the scripts before you run them. Each one explains what it does at the top.

blocks.p: In PowerShell, go to the folder with the scripts. Unblock them (downloaded files are blocked by default), preview with `-WhatIf`, then run the seed:

Sign in with your lab admin account and accept the permissions prompt. The script shows the tenant name and asks you to type its domain. It then creates 7 users in Pacific Crest Logistics (Rolevara lab) and 9 security groups, and saves `rolevara-lab-state.json` in the same folder. Keep that file.

run.title: Work the six tickets in the Entra admin center

blocks.p: Open [entra.microsoft.com](https://entra.microsoft.com/) and go to **Users** and **Groups**. The access matrix and runbook are on the [Policy & matrix](#/policy) page.
The export signs in with read-only permissions and reads only the lab users. It writes `rolevara-lab-export.json`:
Then open the **Upload results** tab. You can fix things in Entra and export again as often as you like.
This deletes only the users and groups the seed created, and only while they still carry the lab tag. Add `-Purge` to also empty them from the recycle bin.

trouble: "Running scripts is disabled on this system"

Run `Unblock-File .\*.ps1`, then allow scripts for this PowerShell window only: `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass`. See [about Execution Policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_execution_policies).
Run the install command on the Setup tab. In Windows PowerShell 5.1, install only those four modules rather than the full Microsoft.Graph module, which can exceed 5.1's function limit.
The sign-in asks for admin approval
Sign in with an admin of the lab tenant. The first run asks you to consent to permissions for Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools.
The seed stops on tenants with more than 50 users so it can't touch a real organization. If the tenant really is a lab, run it with `-LabTenant`.
"A group named … already exists" or "A user … already exists"
A previous lab is still there. Run `.\Remove-RolevaraLab.ps1` from the folder with the state file, or delete those objects in the admin center, then seed again.

Your account needs User Administrator and Groups Administrator, or Global Administrator. See [Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference).
Revoking sessions or resetting a password didn't count
These are read from timestamps that can take a minute to update. Wait, then run the export again.
The export says a user "was not found"
The user was deleted. The runbook disables accounts instead, so that ticket scores 0. Remove the lab and seed it again to retry.
The upload says the file isn't a lab export
Upload `rolevara-lab-export.json`, not the state file. If you edited it, export again.
